verdicts.tldr: gnoweb's own rendered @mention links now land on 404s the new gate produces
verdicts.details: ext_mentions.go:28 is `^@([A-Za-z0-9_]{3,90})(?:[^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)` and lines 84 and 114 are the only sites in the tree that write a /u/ href. The gate the diff installs is `reUsername = gno.Re_name.Compile()` plus `maxUsernameLen = 64`, and Re_name is documented at mempackage.go:70 as `separators (_ or -) only between alphanumerics, never consecutive, never trailing`. The package's own golden output, user_mentions.md.txtar:13, pins `<a href="/u/user_with_many_________underscores_and_numbers_12345">`: 52 characters, so the length cap is not the blocker, but the nine consecutive underscores are, and that page now answers 404 where the merge base rendered 200. The other direction is pinned in the same golden at line 14, `you cannot mention user like @not-user` rendered unlinked, so a hyphenated name that Re_name and r/sys/users both accept never gets a mention link at all. Fix: sweep ext_mentions.go onto the same rule the handler now enforces, gno.Re_name plus the 64 cap for names and crypto.AddressFromBech32 for addresses, and regenerate the golden.

verdicts.tldr: the shape check runs first, so a namespace holding packages 404s when its name is over 64 characters
verdicts.details: GetUserView applies the shape check and returns before buildContributions is ever called, so the `namespace with packages` arm the godoc promises is really `shape AND packages`. The 64 is the registry's cap, store.gno:30 `const maxNameLen = 64`, not a VM rule: Re_gnoUserPkgPath binds its USER component to Re_name with no length limit (mempackage.go:49-54), so a 65-character lowercase namespace is a legal package path. On a chain where r/sys/names is not enabled the verifier passes everything through, verifier.gno:226 `if !isEnabled { return true }`, so such a namespace is deployable on gnodev and on any local test node, and its packages then vanish from /u/. Fix: run buildContributions first and apply the shape check only on the arm that needs it, the r/sys/users lookup. The ordering is settled by the lines; the deploy half was not exercised here, so the reachable instance stands on the absence of a length bound rather than on a run.

verdicts.tldr: the mention rule and the page gate disagree, so rendered mentions 404 and hyphenated users are never linked
verdicts.details: Both directions hold on the read. Producer side: the mention pattern links consecutive underscores and names of 65 to 90 characters, both of which the new gate rejects, and the package's own golden pins one such href, so a realm's rendered mention now answers 404 where the merge base rendered a page. Consumer side: reUserNamespace at keeper.go:1665 is `^[~_a-zA-Z0-9/-]+$` and Re_name admits a hyphen between alphanumerics, but the mention pattern's trailing `[^A-Za-z0-9_-]` guard cannot match `@foo-bar` at all, with no shorter backtrack available under the `{3,90}` floor, and the golden pins that too. One sub-clause of the candidate does not hold: a leading digit or underscore was never served, because reGnolandPath is `^/[rpu]/([a-z][a-z0-9_/-]*)*$` and IsUser is false for /u/_alice and /u/1alice at the merge base as well. Fix: sweep the mention patterns onto gno.Re_name and crypto.AddressFromBech32 in the same change that installs them in the handler.

verdicts.tldr: an address namespace is a real deploy target, so the contributions query is not structurally empty
verdicts.details: The candidate rests on `a package path's second segment is a namespace granted by r/sys/names and can never be address-shaped`. r/sys/names grants exactly that: the personal-address namespace is the verifier's Path 1, `gno.land/{p,r}/{ADDRESS}/**`, matched by `addr.String() == namespace` and returning true before any registered-name lookup. Re_name also admits a bech32 address, which is lowercase alphanumeric starting with a letter, so such a path is legal to the VM as well. The live query the finder ran returns empty for that one address because that account has deployed nothing, not because the prefix cannot match. Applying the proposed fix would delete every contribution from the profile of an account that deploys under its own address, which is the only namespace a user without a registered name has.

verdicts.tldr: an unknown username now costs a VM evaluation on a system realm where it used to cost an early return
verdicts.details: The RPC count is unchanged and the work is not. vm/qrender reaches the same helper as vm/qeval, and that helper returns at `pv == nil` before any allocator or machine exists, so the merge base's query on the absent /r/<name>/home stopped there. The head asks the same helper about /r/sys/users, which exists, so the gas meter, two allocators, the machine and the parse of `ResolveName(...)` all run for every unknown name. /u/<name> is unauthenticated, uncached and crawler-reachable, so a scan over random names pays that per request. The asymmetry is settled by the lines; how much heavier it is was not measured here, so the size of the effect is open. Fix: state the shape change in the description's table, and consider a short negative cache or a cheaper existence probe for the unknown-name path.

verdicts.tldr: the new Eval boundary pushes expression safety onto callers and no test would catch a caller that skips it
verdicts.details: Every code fact the candidate states holds: the godoc says expr is the caller's to keep safe, rpcClient.Eval formats it into the qeval data with no check, and MockClient.Eval and stubClient.Eval ignore expr entirely. There is one production caller and it does validate, through the gate and %q, so nothing in the tree is exploitable today and no run reproduces a failure. What would confirm it is a second caller formatting untrusted input into expr; until one exists this is a shape of the interface, not a defect. Fix: validate inside rpcClient.Eval, or narrow the interface to the query the handler actually needs, a ResolveName lookup rather than an arbitrary expression.

verdicts.tldr: two route assertions depend on genesis registrations that nothing links back to them
verdicts.details: The chain under TestRoutes comes from genesis_txs.jsonl, which carries six RegisterUser calls. moul001 and zoo_ma123 each appear in the whole tree exactly twice, once in that genesis file and once in this test, and neither has a package, so both routes run only through the new qeval branch. Editing or dropping either registration turns the gnoweb package red on a route table that says nothing about where the names come from, and the genesis file carries no note that a gnoweb test depends on them. Fix: name genesis_txs.jsonl in the comment above the two routes, so the reader who edits the genesis file finds the dependency.
